newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberal leader repeats EMU conspiracy charge.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberal leader repeats EMU conspiracy charge.

text.p: Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown on Tuesday repeated accusations that his principal political opponents were conspiring against the British people by refusing to say whether they would enter a single European currency.

In his keynote speech to the party's annual conference, Ashdown said that at the forthcoming general election, "Britain will be asked to vote without knowing what it is voting for. That is a conspiracy perpetrated on the British people by their politicians," he said.
Ashdown's is the only party so far to have said it wants Britain to join a single currency provided it and the so-called core countries qualify to do so.
"If Britain is able to join a single currency and chooses not to, we will pay the price in higher interest rates, higher inflation, lower investment and lost influence," Ashdown said.
"Every British family will lose around 10 pounds a week. And the City of London could lose out completely as Europe's first financial centre."
"The Liberal Democrats are in no doubt. A single currency would be good for Europe. And if it comes and Britain can be a part of it, Britain should be a part of it."
Ashdown repreated his commitment to giving Britons a vote in a referendum before Britain did join the new currency, however,

"With the Liberal Democrats strong in the next Parliament, Britain will have a clear path to follow in Europe and people will have their say," he said. "Without, we will continue to pay the price for the muddle and confusion of two divided parties."
